name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the VISUAL PRESENTATION of the interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment

name: Facet
text: To enhance the visual presentation of our interface, I propose we implement a dynamic, interactive dashboard that utilizes real-time data visualization. This approach prioritizes clarity and engagement, allowing users to easily interpret complex information through intuitive charts and graphs. The trade-off here is that we may require additional resources to develop these dynamic elements, but the resulting improved user experience and enjoyment will significantly outweigh that investment, ultimately driving user satisfaction and uptake.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold on. A "dynamic, interactive dashboard" sounds flashy, but what if our users don’t *need* real-time data? If the interface is for internal ops or slow-moving analytics, that liveliness could just mean noise—distracting from the actual decisions they’re trying to make. Instead, what if we tested a *static but smart* summary view first? The real risk here is over-engineering for engagement when clarity might just need better defaults. Settle it by asking users: do they *actually* need to poke at the data, or just see the answer?
